verses.1: Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, "Did God indeed say, 'You shall not eat from any tree of the garden'?"
verses.2: And the woman said to the serpent, "We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden;
verses.3: but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God has said, 'You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.'"
verses.4: And the serpent said to the woman, "You shall not surely die.
verses.5: For God knows that in the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."
verses.6: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of its fruit and ate; and she also gave to her husband with her, and he ate.
verses.7: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
verses.8: And they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
verses.9: And the LORD God called to Adam and said to him, "Where are you?"
verses.10: And he said, "I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself."
verses.11: And He said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?"
verses.12: And Adam said, "The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate."
verses.13: And the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."
verses.14: And the LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock and above every beast of the field. On your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
verses.15: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He shall crush your head, and you shall bruise his heel."
verses.16: To the woman He said, "I will greatly multiply your pain in childbearing; in pain you shall bring forth children. Your desire shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you."
verses.17: And to Adam He said, "Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat of it,' cursed is the ground because of you; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
verses.18: Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
verses.19: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, till you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return."
verses.20: And Adam called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.
verses.21: And the LORD God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin and clothed them.
verses.22: And the LORD God said, "Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also of the tree of life and eat, and live forever—"
verses.23: therefore the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he was taken.
verses.24: He drove out the man, and at the east of the garden of Eden He placed the cherubim and a flaming sword that turned every way to guard the way to the tree of life.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
